item.title: How to Implement and Understand Exceptions Under the Hood
item.description:
How to Implement and Understand Exceptions Under the Hood

Exceptions are a fundamental part of modern programming languages, enabling developers to handle errors gracefully and maintain control over their code’s execution flow. Surprisingly, many programmers take this powerful feature for granted, often not delving into their implementation details. This prompts an intriguing inquiry: How are exceptions implemented under the hood?

I primarily work with languages like Java, C, C#, Python, and C++. I find the implementation of exceptions fascinating, especially in C++, where you can throw virtually anything. It also piques my interest to explore how one might create a system for exceptions using only the constructs available in C, closely mirroring assembly. Furthermore, I’ve heard rumors suggesting that some Google teams forgo exceptions in favor of performance. Is this speculation grounded in truth? Can substantial programming tasks be achieved without leveraging exceptions?

item.title: Solved: How Ruby and Python Differ - Key Features and Characteristics
item.description:
An In-Depth Comparison: How Ruby and Python Differ in Essential Features

The ongoing debate about the differences between Ruby and Python can be tedious and often subjective, leading to unproductive discussions. Instead of delving into opinions on which language is superior, this post aims to identify and explore the objective features that distinguish Ruby from Python. Here, we will highlight unique characteristics, providing practical examples to illustrate how each feature is implemented in both languages.
